title: Signal Detection Theory for Concept Probes: Separating Sensitivity from Bias

original_idea.body: Apply signal detection theory (d', criterion, ROC) to re-examine the probes-beat-judges claim. Inference-only on labeled benchmarks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: re-examining probe-vs-judge with SDT informs monitor threshold-setting, but catastrophic-risk link is indirect (level 3).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: SDT/ROC is a few lines on labeled benchmarks; motivated beginner feasible (level 5).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (d'/criterion decomposition vs judge), few dependencies (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly careful-evaluation work on open models and labeled benchmarks (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: SDT analysis on cached probe scores, near free-tier (level 5).

novelty.reasoning: SDT is standard but applying it to re-examine probe-vs-judge may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: SDT well established; the probe-vs-judge re-examination angle may be open.
